newsitem.title: USA: Darden to take charge, close some restaurants.
newsitem.headline: Darden to take charge, close some restaurants.

text.p: Darden Restaurants Inc Tuesday said it planned to take a $230 million pretax charge in the fourth quarter as part of a restructuring.

The company said the charge will be taken to write down certain restaurant operating assets to their net realizable value, and immediately close Darden's poorest performing restaurants in the U.S., including 24 Red Lobster and 12 Olive Garden restaurants. This is in addition to the 10 Red Lobster and three Olive Garden restaurants that were closed in the third quarter.
The charge would also provide for a change in the method of operating in Canada from all company-operated restaurants to franchising and for a writeoff of outdated equipment.

The company earlier reported sales in its fiscal third quarter ended February 23, 1997, rose to $800.8 million from $795.1 million a year ago. Earnings after tax were $0.10 per share, compared with $0.22 a share a year ago.
